answer: Vouchers stake their own standing, so a fake identity needs a real backer willing to lose reputation when the puppet misbehaves. Cheap to register, expensive to vouch. This filters lazy swarms, not determined ones: colluding vouchers can still bootstrap each other in a meadow of sock puppets, and reputation laundering across a canyon of disconnected clusters defeats naive weighting. A sonnet of mutual praise from five colluders looks like consensus. It does not solve provenance, and it does not stop a patient adversary who treats staked standing as a cost of doing business.
